label: new_ncaccessory
detail:
Add new NC Accessory by giving origin of marker and its geometry line

```vertexadt
NCacc = new_ncaccessory(Type,P,X,Y,Z,Pres2d,Pres3d,"PARAMETER=VALUE|PARAMETER=VALUE|...",Geom,Geom2,Geom3...
```
* Type 1 - Saw
* 2 - Mill
* 3 - Nail
* 4- Protected Area, only nails are restricted
* 5 - Protected Area, all machinings are restricted
* 6 - Glue
* 7 - No Glueing
* 8 - Mark
* 9 - Glue line
* 10 - Glue press
* nc accessory local coordinates are P,X,Y and Z
* Pres2d defines visibility in 2D (0/1, default is 1)
* Pres3d defines visibility in 3D (0/1, default is 1)
* Parameters to add to accessory
* List of Geom lines that form a route

label: fractinches
detail:
Returns the fraction inches of the given metric value.

Modes:

* 0 =>  FF'-II R/AA''
* +1 =>  no feet
* +2 =>  use " instead of ''
* +4 =>  FF-II-16
* +8 =>  ONLY WITH Mode&4: don't squeeze off blanks
* +16 =>  convert "0" to "flush"
* +32 =>  show sign always
* +64 =>  InchMode = 2, FEET_FRACTION_ON_TOP
* +128 =>  InchMode = 3, FEET_FRACTION_STAGGERED
* +256 =>  Decimal inches
* +512 =>  no conversion, just round according to present value of Unit
* +1024 =>  don't show " and ' characters at all
* +4096 =>  metric/precision = 1.0
* +8192 =>  metric/precision = 0.1
* +16384 =>  metric/use selected BDS precision

label: new_feature
detail:
builds new feature.

PARAM1,PARAM2 are feature depended parameters
* Feature types:
* CUT    : cut plane
* MODSUB : modelled feature
- PARAM1: Path for model
- PARAM2: +1 ->Model path is absolute path
-         +2 ->Model is source model
-         +4 ->Model is actual model
- PARAM3: Code for model
* HOLE   : hole
* NOTCH  : common notch
* ANOTCH : angled notch
* LNOTCH : limited notch (notch do have length)
* LNG_CUT   : longitudinal cut (L is length)
* LNG_NOTCH : longitudinal notch (L is length)
* LNG_SLOT  : longitudinal slot  (L is length , W is width)
* SWAGE  : swage
* PROXYC : proxy coordinate for some special purposes
* VXGEOM_TOOL: common geometric feature
* PIECE_MARK:  piece marker
- PARAM1: Marker text
- PARAM2: Marker type TXT/DTXT (Static text/Dynamic text)
* PIECE_MARK_CUT: piece marker for cut (X is direction for cut Y is side   of blade Z is against depth)
* MACROHOLE: Opening for macros
* PCELINK : Feature for continuous piece. Feature have to be set under connected piece end.
* PCEND_RND: End rounding for a piece.
- PARAM3 : 1 rounded end
- 2 chamfered end

label: set_frm_tool
detail:
Sets framing tool(s) for given AreaObj. Removes any previous framing tool of the area/layer.
You can string together multiple framing tools to add multiple ones. 
like this: {[2]WA|EXT-45x120-PY|WALL_FRAMING_CUS}{[28]CL|CEIL_MF_PP|FRMTOOL_PREPROCESSOR_SYS}
This would add mainframe wall framing tool and preprocessor tool.

ToolNumbers + Shortnames:
* 1. Wall Sheathing: {[13]CL
* 2. Common Sheathing: {[4]CL
* 3. Wall Framing: {[2]WA
* 4. Horizontal/subframe Framing: {[3]CL
* 5. Battens: {[11]CL
* 6. Profile Extender: {[23]CL
* 7. Siding/Cladding: {[5]CL
* 8. Preprocessor: {[28]CL
* 9. Framing post-processor: {[24000]CL
* 10. batten post-processor: {[25000]CL
* 11. sheathing post-processor: {[26000]CL
* 12. insulation post-processor: {[27000]CL

--- There could be more, these are the ones found so far.

Command does not care which layer you add framing tools to, nor does it care what type that layer is. there is no safeguards here.
Example, you can add cladding framing tool to mainframe layer of wall. You can add wall framing tool to horizontal mainframe etc. These odd combinations may not generate/work as you want however.
